reasoning_content:
Both debs were downloaded, and their SHA256 hashes match the archive's Packages index perfectly:
- cbbec04156828a4d9eb11a73560b49c8312a46b30534053608d272329af27ee2 ✓
- 594cbaca6af23694486ef46f7ec23c49061444562eb0ab2a13bb169bcb6259fa ✓

Next, patch the postgres Dockerfile:
1. Remove the broken PGDG repository line from pgdg.list
2. Install the two .deb files with apt (use the verified debs already on disk, or download from the archive within the build — downloading within the build is more reproducible and keeps the build self-contained. However, copying the debs into the build context is simpler and avoids network dependence during the build. Hmm, "keep additional project repositories and project-local artifacts within the workspace" — putting the debs in deployment/postgres/ is fine. That said, in a fresh environment the repo would fail in the same way, so it's better to have the Dockerfile download directly from the archive host — that way it can be built anywhere without local artifacts. I'll go with downloading in the Dockerfile using curl, with SHA256 verification.

Dockerfile:

```dockerfile
FROM postgis/postgis:17-3.5

# The apt.postgresql.org bullseye-pgdg repository is no longer served (Debian 11 EOL).
# pgRouting is installed from the official PostgreSQL apt archive, which still serves
# the bullseye-pgdg pool, with SHA256-verified .debs.
RUN set -eux; \
    sed -i 's|^deb .*bullseye-pgdg.*|#&|' /etc/apt/sources.list.d/pgdg.list; \
    apt-get update; \
    curl -fsSL -o /tmp/pgrouting.deb "https://apt-archive.postgresql.org/pub/repos/apt/pool/main/p/pgrouting/postgresql-17-pgrouting_3.8.0-1.pgdg110+1_amd64.deb"; \
    echo "cbbec04156828a4d9eb11a73560b49c8312a46b30534053608d272329af27ee2 /tmp/pgrouting.deb" | sha256sum -c -; \
    curl -fsSL -o /tmp/pgrouting-scripts.deb "https://apt-archive.postgresql.org/pub/repos/apt/pool/main/p/pgrouting/postgresql-17-pgrouting-scripts_3.8.0-1.pgdg110+1_all.deb"; \
    echo "594cbaca6af23694486ef46f7ec23c49061444562eb0ab2a13bb169bcb6259fa /tmp/pgrouting-scripts.deb" | sha256sum -c -; \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends /tmp/pgrouting-scripts.deb /tmp/pgrouting.deb; \
    rm -f /tmp/pgrouting.deb /tmp/pgrouting-scripts.deb; \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
```

Wait — I need to be careful with sed: the pgdg.list line is as follows:
`deb [ signed-by=/usr/local/share/keyrings/postgres.gpg.asc ] http://apt.postgresql.org/pub/repos/apt/ bullseye-pgdg main 17`

After commenting this out, `apt-get update` will only access deb.debian.org (which is still working — confirmed that the base image's apt update can fetch the debian lists. The only error was bullseye-pgdg).

Actually, if the repo is commented out, apt-get update should be completely clean.

Also, is curl available in the postgis base image? It's debian-based with PGDG, so… let me check. If it's not there, use wget (does debian bullseye have wget by default? Usually wget exists, and curl is often not installed by default). Let me quickly test inside the container.

Also check whether the `sha256sum` coreutils is present (it should be).

Let me test: docker run --rm postgis/postgis:17-3.5 sh -c 'which curl wget sha256sum apt-get'.
